title: Women, Culture, and Development
abstract: This volume, which grows out of The Quality of Life (eds. Martha Nussbaum and Amartya Sen, 1993), combines philosophical inquiry with economic concerns regarding women's equality in the developing world. Adopting Amartya Sen's capability framework, international contributors tackle issues of cultural relativism vs. cultural imperialism on the one hand, and questions of local traditions vs. universalist critical judgement on the other. The chief aim of this work is to critically explore the relationship between culture and justice as pertinent to women's development, with special attention paid to cultural sensitivity but without compromising the clarity of rational judgement in cases where women's capabilities are at stake. Building upon the practical and philosophical implications of the lived experience of women from a variety of cultures, the authors theorize the pragmatics of economic development beyond utility towards a vision of gender equality. This book is a must‐read for anyone interested in the ethics of women's economic development.

Full narrative

Women, Culture, and Development by Martha C. Nussbaum and Jonathan Glover was published by Oxford University PressOxford in 1995. Conceptually, the work connects to Judgement, CLARITY, Relativism, Economic Justice and Cultural relativism.

OpenAlex records 625 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2005 with 51 citing works. Notable citing venues include Cambridge University Press eBooks, Palgrave Macmillan UK eBooks and Hypatia. The citing works include 256 journal articles and 241 book chapters. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia.

Open Library reports a combined count of 3 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Gender equality among the Sustainable Development Goals.
